title: build.py newProblems schema mismatch
first_prompt: Let's address issues with build.py from last verification run. Summary: `newProblems` schema mismatch between `build.py` and the schema. Next, the submitter should reconcile those two files and resubm

commits.summary: The result schema takes what build.py writes for a boundary contract's new problems and a vacuous symbolic proof; examples 111-119 and 144 resubmitted (verification pending)
commits.body:
The last verification run failed examples 111 to 119 on result.json validation: build.py writes newProblems (the `!` lines a regenerated B12 contract gains) and the schema did not list it. The schema also allowed coverage only in its TLC form, while build.py writes {vacuous, reason} for a regression or property proof the tool reports as vacuous, so example 144's pending job would have failed the same way. The schema now lists newProblems as an array of strings, and coverage as null, the TLC object, or {vacuous: true, reason}. Checked by validating all 105 committed result.json files against it (all valid) and synthetic B12 and vacuous B9 results (valid), with a missing reason and a non-array newProblems rejected.

Jobs resubmitted at this commit: 20261104-131020-example-111..117, 20261104-131021-example-118, -119 and -144 (the never-run 20261104-124827-example-144 job, pinned to the old schema, removed). The other failures in the run (example 036's patch no longer applying to Mica, example 109's replay of a static field) are not about the schema and are left.

commits.summary: The Java contract verifier leaves another tool's contract alone, so Box Office's build passes again
commits.body: Box Office's contracts module applies both contract plugins: the behavioural/capability one (examples/tools/contracts) and the boundaries one (jvmcontract). Since that module gained a boundaries.contract for the wire types, the Java verifier read it as a behavioural contract, and :contracts:verifyContracts, and with it the app's check, failed with 'boundaries.contract: not a case: kind: boundaries'. An Opus 5.5 session noticed it on Nov 3 while measuring memory caps and left it open. The verifier now skips any .contract file whose first line is a kind: header (Contract.kind), a behavioural contract having none.
Brings the published traces up to this point: conversation that came after a session's last commit, and sessions with no commit of their own.

commits.summary: Record verification results for 35 jobs: examples 111-120, 124, 125, 132, 133 pass; 21 B9 jobs fail on tool or patch mismatches, not verdicts
commits.body: The runner ran all 35 queued jobs (2 workers, 5 GiB). Passes: 120, 124, 125, 132, 133 (B9, own checker, seconds) and 111-119 (B12, about 1m40s each, resubmitted after the result schema fix; every verdict as expected). Their outputs were applied. 21 B9 jobs failed in 0.2-5 s with no proof attempted, so these are findings about the submitted commits, not about the changes under test: 121, 122, 130, 134 and 135 (and per their logs 123, 131) fail in the CLI: the jvmcontract built from lib/ at the job's commit rejects an argument build.py passes (e.g. --before-arguments, or a missing required --unchanged-unless). 128 and 129: the example's patch does not change BatchCommit.java. 126, 127, 136-145: the checker reports 'cannot be verified' (instance method on a record, char[]/int[] parameter outside the fragment), so the expected verdict is not reached. Each of those needs a resubmit at a commit where examples/tools/build.py and lib/ agree.

commits.summary: The pipeline builds jvmcontract from each job's own lib/ instead of reusing the last binary, and build.py takes the excerpt of a method moved out of a deleted file; 26 B9 jobs resubmitted (verification pending)
commits.body:
Of the last run's 35 jobs, 21 B9 jobs failed with what looked like mismatches between build.py and lib/ (rejected flags, instance methods and arrays outside the fragment). The real cause: the pipeline builds jvmcontract in one CARGO_TARGET_DIR shared by all jobs, from a git archive extraction whose files are dated at their commit, older than the binary any earlier job left there, so cargo rebuilt nothing. Thirteen lib/ trees got one identical binary, built at 08:27, which did not know --before-arguments. The five B9 jobs that passed (120, 124, 125, 132, 133) ran on that stale binary as well, so their results, applied in the previous commit, are replaced when these jobs run. build_jvmcontract now dates lib/ at the build's start, so cargo rebuilds the crate, and refuses a binary older than the build. The poisoned cache under verification/.state/tools/jvmcontract was cleared. Reproduced in the scratchpad: lib/ at cf74bb4c then at 198d4317 in one target directory, the second build took 0.03 s and lacked --before-arguments; with the dating it rebuilt in 49 s and had it. verification/test_pipeline.py passes (15 tests).

Examples 128 and 129 failed separately: their patch deletes the subject file BatchCommit.java and moves the method into the new record Batch.java, and excerpts() in examples/tools/build.py read only '+++ b/' paths, so it found no hunk. It now reads the before side from the '--- a/' path and the after side from the '+++ b/' path, and when the patch deletes the subject file it takes the after side from the file of the symbol's class. Checked against the previous version on every example with a patch: 138 give identical excerpts, and 128 and 129 now give BatchCommit.java before and Batch.java after.

Jobs resubmitted at this commit with estimates of 2m and 1G (4m for 142): 20261104-140707-example-120 through -127, 20261104-140708-example-128 through -135, 20261104-140709-example-136 through -143 and -145, and 20261104-140717-example-144.

commits.summary: Record verification results for 26 resubmitted B9 jobs: 24 pass, 128 and 129 fail because the patch no longer applies to Tests.java
commits.body: After the pipeline began building jvmcontract from each job's own lib/, the 26 B9 jobs resubmitted in 9325f7ee ran with 2 workers and 4 GiB. 24 passed in 4-19 s (peak under 440 MiB) with the verdict each example expects, and their outputs were applied: 120-127 and 130-145 (121-123 related proofs, 124/125/132/133/138/141/142/145 proved or refuted by the own checker), 134-137, 139, 140, 143, 144. 128 and 129 failed in 0.2 s: the example's patch no longer applies: its hunk in crosscut/Tests.java was cut before WindowTest was added to the class list, so git apply rejects it and build.py stops before any proof; that is the submitter's to fix.

commits.summary: Examples 128 and 129's patches apply again: their Tests.java hunk rebased past WindowTest; both resubmitted (verification pending)
commits.body: 128 and 129 failed in the last run at git apply: their patch renames BatchCommitTest to BatchTest in Crosscut's test runner list, and the Window record kernel (examples 134/135) had since inserted WindowTest into that list, so the hunk's context no longer matched. The hunk now starts at line 24 with WindowTest as context, and its index line names the current blobs. Checked: git apply --check passes for both, and each patch applied to a copy of Crosscut compiles and passes the module's tests (48 and 49 tests, 0 failed). Every other example's patch still applies except 036's on Mica, a known separate drift.

commits.summary: Example 036's patch regenerated on the current SwitchLowering.java, so it applies again (verification pending)
commits.body: 036 failed in the Mica rerun at git apply: the patch was written before commit lrptsmzx added two lines to the class comment and a sortPairs method after useTable, so its hunk started two lines early and its closing context assumed the class ended after useTable. The patch was regenerated by making the same edit on the current file (useTable's four cost variables narrowed from long to int); its removed and added lines are identical to the old patch's. Checked: git apply --check passes, and Mica with the patch compiles and passes its tests (71 tests, 0 failed). Every example's patch in the repo now applies to the current tree.
